{{Infobox football league season |competition=[[Uzbek League]] |season=1993 |winners= [[Neftchi Farg'ona]] |relegated= [[FK Samarqand-Dinamo|Dinamo Samarqand]]
[[FK Kosonsoy|Kushon Kosonsoy]] |continentalcup1= |continentalcup1 qualifiers= |continentalcup2= |continentalcup2 qualifiers= |league topscorer= [[Rustam Durmonov]] [[Neftchi Farg'ona]] (26 goals) |biggest home win= |biggest away win= |highest scoring= |matches= |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest losses= |highest attendance = |lowest attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1992 Uzbek League|1992]] |nextseason=[[1994 Uzbek League|1994]] }} The '''1993 [[Uzbek League]] season''' was the second edition of top level football in [[Uzbekistan]] since independence from the [[Soviet Union]] in 1992. [[FK Neftchi Farg'ona|Neftchi Farg'ona]] once again won the league and the championship outright this time after previously sharing with [[FC Pakhtakor Tashkent|Pakhtakor Tashkent]] the season before. On winning the championship, Nefchi also qualified for the next edition of the [[AFC Champions League]], the first time a club side from Uzbekistan would play in AFC competitions. They would also enter the [[1994 Commonwealth of Independent States Cup]] a competition for former members of the Soviet Union. [[FC Pakhtakor|Pakhtakor Tashkent]] won the [[Uzbek Cup#1993|1993 Uzbek Cup]] and would take their place in the [[1994–95 Asian Cup Winners' Cup]]. [[FK Samarqand-Dinamo|Dinamo Samarqand]] and [[FK Kosonsoy|Kushon Kosonsoy]] were relegated. ==Teams== Shahrixonchi Shahrixon, Kimyogar Olmaliq and Surxon Termiz were relegated to the [[Uzbekistan 1-Division]] in the 1992 season campaign and were replaced by Shifokor Guliston and Politotdel Tashkent. During the off season, three teams decided to change name: * ''Kosonsoychi Kosonsoy'' changed name to ''[[FK Kosonsoy|Kushon Kosonsoy]]'' * ''Maroqand Samarqand'' changed name to ''Dinamo Samarqand''
